constraint_decided_it: Every property A proposes holds inside its declared domain/range (P41 E17->E1, P42 E17->E55, P14 E7->E39, P17 E7->E1, with E17 IsA E13 IsA E7), and every quotation A gives verifies (t0483, t1306, Issue 333 'decided to incorporate the models for Activity Plans in the CRMsoc', Issue 419 'CRMact will be a stand-alone extension'). B attributes a verbatim sentence to Issue 166 -- 'dealing with instances of E4 in the future (if they exist at all) will be subject of extensions of the CRM, and not part of the scope of CRM' -- that appears nowhere: Issue 166's register text is only 'To be included in Issue 161 documentation activities. Crete 18/05/2011', and whitespace-normalised grep over crm-sig.mbox and crm_issues.json returns 0 hits for every fragment of it.
better_modelling: Three-way split, not two. (1) The disposal-review decision is retrospective and in scope: E17 Type Assignment (IsA E13 IsA E7), P14 carried out by the records officer (E39), P41 classified the file, P42 assigned an E55 disposition type, P4 has time-span the review date; P17 was motivated by the statutory instrument (E31/E30), or P2 has type / P21 had general purpose on the assignment to distinguish statutory requirement from curatorial judgement; a carried-out destruction is a later E6 Destruction, P13 destroyed the E22/E84 file. (2) The retention schedule *as an existing document* is in CRMbase now, not exiled to CRMact: E29 Design or Procedure covers 'documented plans for the execution of actions ... for shaping or guiding the execution of an instance of E7 Activity', reached from the review by P33 used specific technique; E87 Curation Activity's own scope note presupposes exactly this by speaking of items 'added or removed from an instance of E78 Curated Holding' 'following an implicit or explicit curation plan', which is what an archival retention schedule is. (3) Only the not-yet-occurred review *event* and its next-review date fall outside CRMbase -- that is the CRMact/CRMsoc boundary of Issues 333/419, and it does not sweep the schedule document out with it.
reasoning: Both answers reach the same substantive split (decision retrospective and modellable, future review event outside CRMbase) and both support that split from real sources, so the separation is evidential and granular, not directional. A is suboptimal: its property applications all check out against declared domain and range, but it rejects E87 on the false ground that no curated holding is involved -- an archival series is an E78 -- and rejects E29 for the retention schedule wholesale, when E29's scope note ('plans ... for shaping or guiding the execution of an instance of E7 Activity') covers the schedule as an extant document; only the future event is out of scope. B is unsupported: its load-bearing Issue 166 quotation is absent from the register and from the whole archive, and it compounds this by declaring in_scope False for a case whose retrospective half B itself then models, against Doerr's own reading in t1306 that for archival records 'CRM is very adequate, and the above should not be difficult to be modeled'.
